messages:
anna: quick flag vs rollout policy question — a customer hit an edge where a feature flag in the console enabled a new model, but the rollout policy on the service had a canary that should have limited traffic. which wins?

mike: do we have an incident link? is this the console flag overriding runtime policy or the other way?

anna: no incident, just a support ticket. screenshot shows console flag = ON for org, but routing shows 100% to new model (should have been 5%).

sophia: short answer: current code paths are messy. flags are evaluated by the API gateway (fast path) and rollout policies by the router later. so whichever runs first can effectively control routing.

jake: that explains it. we have three relevant layers: global org flags, service-level rollout policies (priority-based), and route-level feature toggles. we never standardized precedence.

natalie: suggestion: introduce explicit precedence rules: enforced policies (guards) > rollout policies > feature flags, where flags are intended as soft/experiments.

mike: curious — for A/B splits we rely on rollout policies for % splits and stickiness. feature flags often have % rollout too. who owns the split calculation?

sophia: currently both can express percentages. messy when both present. propose: only rollout policies can define routing splits; flags can map to variants but must not set traffic%.

anna: +1 to that. also we need the console and API to show the "effective" routing config for a given request so it's obvious what will apply.

jake: API idea: POST /evaluate-rollout with request context -> returns resolved variant + provenance (policy_id or flag_id). console shows that for debug.

natalie: and telemetry: tag every served response with source:policy|flag and rule_id so we can retroactively see which rule served traffic.

anna: mini-proposal for precedence wording (we can debate): 1) enforced guard policies (hard deny/force) 2) rollout policies (routing/splits) 3) feature flags (soft toggles that map to features but not override enforced routing).

mike: edge case: a feature flag used as a guard via "enforced": true in console — we should normalize that to a policy under the hood. otherwise ownership is ambiguous.

sophia: agreed. if console exposes an 'enforced' checkbox for flags, the backend should create/convert to a policy object and set provenance to "generated-from-flag".

jake: UI/UX ask: show a single "effective rules" panel that flattens layers and highlights conflicts with clear source labels. also a small explainer: "policies can enforce routing; flags should not be used to enforce splits".

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: updated rollout-service config for service-alpha (v3)

anna: next steps: i'll draft a short RFC with precedence, conversion rules for enforced flags, API endpoint for evaluation, and telemetry keys.

mike: i'll add a dashboard card to track source:policy vs source:flag over last 30d so we can quantify.

sophia: i'll scope API + router change; jake can help UI.

natalie: thanks — will join RFC review. :thumbsup:
